Quick Start

In this guide, we'll set up a console application and create a simple page with a text input, button and status message. After that, we'll create a similar page using MXML.

Prerequisites

  • .NET SDK: .NET 10.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio or another C# IDE. The commands below also work from a terminal.
  • MelonUI Source: A local checkout of the MelonUI repository.
  • Interactive Terminal: Running the window requires console input and output. Use CaptureText when you only need an offline render.

1. Create the Application

Create a console project and add a reference to MelonUI:

Replace the reference path with the location of your checkout. For example, on Windows this might be D:/Documents/GitHub/MelonUI/MelonUI/MelonUI.csproj. The project reference will also restore the Pastel and Wcwidth dependencies.

Understanding the Code

  • ConsoleWindowManager: Manages the console window and runs the input/render loop.
  • MUIPage.Children: Holds the controls on the page. Each control is added once.
  • TextBox: Contains the name entered by the user. The label requires a height of 5 rows when a border is shown.
  • Button.OnPressed: Updates the status TextBlock using the current input value.
  • Y: Sets the vertical position. MUIPage does not automatically stack its children.
  • RunAsync: Runs until Stop is called or the cancellation token is cancelled.

3. Run and Test

You should see a page like this:

  1. Enter a name in the TextBox.
  2. Press Tab to focus the Say hello button.
  3. Press Enter. The status should change to Hello, followed by the name you entered.
  4. Press Escape to stop the window and restore the console.

5. Try the Live MXML Demo

From the MelonUI checkout, you can run the demo to edit markup while viewing the result:

On Windows, the demo creates a file and opens it in Notepad. Save your changes to recompile the page. If there is an error, it will be shown below the last working page. F5 recompiles manually, and Escape closes the preview. The file is kept in the system temp directory after exit.

On other platforms, open the displayed path in your editor.

Using Local Packages

The current code can also build MelonUI 1.0.0 as a local NuGet package. From the repository, run:

Keep nuget.org configured alongside the local source so dependencies can be restored. Use -CoreOnly with Verify-Packages.ps1 if you do not need the shader package. These commands create local packages; they do not publish a public NuGet release.

The NuGet package includes the binding generator. If you are using project references and adding custom bindable fields, see the generator setup.
